title: The Moon and the Mirror
author: Sankar Narayan Mallick
text:
My wish is one in a million
milling around you,
of one among the
innumerable humans
humming around you.
How does it matter
and how does it bother you,
a tiny wish,
howsoever dear and tender !

After all,
It is not a glance at the moon,
but only at its reflection
which the waters,
wily and effervescent,
may mirror and hold
or hide away or scatter
as per its own strange
spontaneity of a desire.
Touched and tantalised,
there is no end to looking
at the river that you are !

Let me go home,
in a loss of words,
lonesome,
without looking behind,
in the muted murmur
of a protest to your busy-bee mind
that does not look beyond.

Let the music play on,
on the river
and on the moon.
Lonesome,
in the softest of silence,
let me go home.
stanzas: My wish is one in a million
and how does it bother you,
It is not a glance at the moon,
there is no end to looking
at the river that you are !
of a protest to your busy-bee mind
